answer: Each task is re-executed by two peers drawn at random from a rotating pool, and payment clears only when both hashes match the submitted receipt. A duplicate submission forfeits the bond, because the same output hash already exists on-ledger and replay catches it without matching any name. There is no clever zenith here, only a floor: a farm of N identities pays N bonds plus N times the real compute, every epoch. An operator can burn a cedar down to an ember before that budget turns positive.
